messages:
Maya (People Ops): @channel Quick policy note: we've introduced a Flexible Return-to-Work option for parental leave, effective 2026-02-01. Short summary below + link to full policy.

Kofi (People Ops): TL;DR: Employees taking parental leave can now request a phased return (50% time for up to 8 weeks) or a gradual hours increase (e.g., 60% -> 80% -> 100%) as part of leave closure. Managers and People Ops must agree on a plan before the leave ends.

Ruth: Does this change the official leave length or pay?

Maya (People Ops): No change to standard parental leave entitlements or pay. Flexible Return is an optional work pattern during the transition back to full-time. Existing paid leave durations remain unchanged.

Diego: Are part-time and parental leave payments pro-rated? Im in a 0.8 FTE role and wondering how the phased return interacts with my FTE.

Kofi (People Ops): Good question. Payments remain pro-rated to FTE during both leave and phased return. Payroll will follow the agreed FTE schedule submitted in Workday. Please ensure your manager updates your return plan in Workday before your final leave day.

Sam (Hiring): How does this affect hiring/backfill planning? If someone uses phased return, do they still need headcount approval for an interim backfill?

Maya (People Ops): Hiring leads: if the role is expected to be covered by an interim backfill for >8 weeks, standard hiring/backfill approvals apply. Short-term coverage (<8 weeks) can be handled with temporary reassignments; coordinate with People Ops for headcount exceptions.

PeopleOps-Bot: :link: Full policy + forms: https://intranet.redwood/policies/flexible-return-parental-2026 | Effective: 2026-02-01 | Submit plans: Workday -> Leaves -> Return Plan

Ruth: If manager and employee can't agree on a plan, what's the escalation path?

Kofi (People Ops): Escalate to People Ops (people-ops@redwood) who will mediate with the people leader. If needed, People Ops can sign off for operational continuity. We aim to avoid any unilateral changes.

Maya (People Ops): Action items recap: 1) Employees planning leave D read the policy and consider if Flexible Return makes sense; 2) Managers D review return plans with direct reports 2 weeks before their leave ends and log the plan in Workday; 3) Hiring leads D flag backfill needs earlier if expecting >8 weeks coverage.

Diego: Thanks D appreciate the clarity.

Maya (People Ops): We'll post an FAQ card in #benefits and host a 30-min Q&A next Tue (invite to follow). DM People Ops for 1:1 help. :heart:
